definition: A learning automaton is one type of machine learning algorithm studied since 1970s.
details: Learning automata select their current action based on past experiences from the environment. It will fall into the range of reinforcement learning if the environment is stochastic and a Markov decision process (MDP) is used.

explainer.lead: A learning automaton is a machine learning algorithm that selects its current action based on past experience from the environment, studied since the 1970s. It matters as an early reinforcement-style approach to adaptive decision-making.

tiers.eli5: A simple agent keeps trying actions and, based on how the world responds, gradually favors the actions that worked.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers apply learning automata to adaptive action selection in stochastic environments. A pitfall is that they fall into reinforcement learning territory only when the environment is stochastic and modeled as a Markov decision process.
tiers.paperLevel: The automaton updates its action probabilities from environmental feedback; it falls within reinforcement learning when a stochastic environment is modeled as a Markov decision process. The framework predates modern deep RL and lacks its scalability.

explainer.example: An automaton choosing among several channels learns to favor the channel that most often returns a reward.
